newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO rises on Chinese enquiries.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO rises on Chinese enquiries.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Thursday firmed on reduced regional supplies, tracking a firm swaps market and Chinese demand, traders said.
Traders said more Chinese enquiries were heard boosting market sentiments. China has bought up all available South Korean and Japanese spot cargoes, traders said.
They said more Chinese demand were seen with the tariffs cut, starting November 11, down to 3 percent from 12 percent.
Chinese buyers said more imports were also expected as drought has hit northwest China, spurring more fuel oil imports for power generation to supplement the shortage in hydro power generation.
The China Business Times reported earlier Thursday that drought in northwestern China has hit the regions' hydroelectric output and aggravating power shortages.
South Korean high sulphur fuel oil supplies were also limited as refiners are still running low sulphur crude.
A cargo was heard sold late Thursday at $123.50 for cargoes loading in early December, at least $1 higher from Wednesday's quotes.
In the swaps market, December was bid/asked at $119.50/$120.50, firm from Wednesday's $118/$119.
